Turn notes and PDFs into summaries, flashcards and practice material. This screen shows how the portfolio would explain the project; it is not a live copy of StudyMind.

The problem

Preparing study material can take time away from using it. The project brings document input and structured study output into one workflow.

The decision

Separate the interface, API, provider generation and persistence so the workflow can communicate its current state.

Notes / PDF→FastAPI→Structured material→Saved sets

What the case study would show

Input limits, progress and failure states, consent, review before saving, account boundaries and the tradeoffs behind the architecture. No adoption or learning-impact numbers are assumed.

lotus:
Lotus / UX205 information architecture · Academic research by Hamza Rizvi

A closed card sort tested twenty page labels against five proposed navigation categories. Five participants completed the study; the proposed sitemap contains thirty pages.

Only 1 of 5 participants put “Compare models” in Compare.

The result challenged the original standalone comparison category. It did not prove a replacement structure would work.

What held up

Handbooks & manuals reached Owners for 4 of 5 participants, the clearest agreement in the dataset.

What stayed uncertain

No card reached unanimous agreement. Fifteen of twenty peaked at 2 of 5. Sessions were fast, so the findings remain directional.

From evidence to structure

Retain Owners as a support hub, make Contact us a global utility, investigate comparison inside model pages, clarify purchase labels and retest. The supplied proposed categories remain Models, Compare, Buy & test drive, Owners, and Lotus story.

Read completed report ↗Open sitemap ↗

AI / Machine Learning / Python · PyTorch · Torchvision · Pillow · React · Vite · Tailwind CSS · Radix UI

Co-developed a handwriting recognition project combining a React interface for drawing and image uploads with a custom PyTorch convolutional neural network. The model classifies handwritten characters across 47 output classes. Implemented image preprocessing for inference using grayscale conversion, normalization, and colour inversion, with saved model weights available for local predictions.

The problem

Handwriting recognition typically requires either expensive proprietary APIs or poorly documented open-source models. The goal was to build an end-to-end solution—from data preprocessing to a trained model to a usable web interface—as a learning exercise in the full ML pipeline.

The approach

Built a CNN with PyTorch and Torchvision trained on the EMNIST dataset covering 47 output classes. The React/Vite frontend provides a canvas for freehand drawing and file upload. Images are preprocessed (grayscale conversion, normalization, colour inversion) before being passed to the model for inference.

Inside the project

  • 47-class character classification (letters and digits)
  • Custom CNN trained with PyTorch and Torchvision
  • React + Vite frontend with canvas drawing interface
  • Image preprocessing pipeline: grayscale, normalization, colour inversion
  • Saved model weights for local inference

Full Stack / React · JavaScript · HTML · CSS · Anthropic Claude API · localStorage

Developed a marketing campaign generator that uses the Anthropic Claude API to transform campaign ideas and audience details into structured plans. Generated outputs include messaging, customer journeys, channel strategies, KPIs, and budget recommendations. Implemented tabbed results, campaign refinement, clipboard export, and browser-based storage for saved campaigns.

The problem

Marketing teams and independent creators often lack the resources to produce structured campaign strategies from scratch. The goal was a tool that could turn a brief description into a complete, actionable campaign plan instantly.

The approach

Used React with vanilla CSS for the frontend and the Claude API for generation. Campaign inputs are transformed into structured prompts that instruct Claude to produce a JSON-shaped response covering messaging, channels, KPIs, and budget. Results are displayed in a tabbed interface and persisted via browser localStorage.

Inside the project

  • Claude API integration for structured campaign plan generation
  • Outputs: messaging, customer journeys, channel strategies, KPIs, budget recommendations
  • Tabbed result display with campaign refinement capability

Mobile Development / Swift · SwiftUI · Foundation · Swift Concurrency · iOS

Developed an iOS fitness application using Swift and SwiftUI, combining workout planning, active workout tracking, and nutrition features. Implemented rule-based workout generation using fitness level, training goals, and selected muscle groups to produce exercise plans with sets, repetitions, and rest periods. Organized the application into reusable UI components, data models, and service layers.

The problem

Existing fitness apps are often overcomplicated or rely on subscription paywalls. The goal was a clean, opinionated iOS app that generates effective workout plans without requiring AI APIs or cloud dependencies.

The approach

Built entirely in Swift with SwiftUI for the UI layer. Workout generation uses rule-based logic keyed on fitness level, selected muscle groups, and training goals. The app is structured into UI components, data models, and service layers for maintainability.

Inside the project

  • Rule-based workout generation by fitness level, goals, and muscle groups
  • Active workout tracking with sets, reps, and rest timers
  • Nutrition feature with food logging
  • SwiftUI component architecture with data model and service layer separation

Robotics / Embedded Systems / Python · OpenCV · NVIDIA Jetson Nano · Raspberry Pi Camera · Computer Vision · Embedded Systems

Contributed to a robotics project combining a mobile chassis with a camera-based computer vision system. Integrated a Jetson Nano and Raspberry Pi camera module to process live video for face detection and age estimation. Worked on mechanical assembly and embedded hardware integration to connect the robot's movement platform with its vision subsystem.

The problem

Building an autonomous robot that can detect and classify faces requires tightly coupling a real-time vision pipeline with embedded hardware constraints—low power, limited memory, and physical assembly challenges.

The approach

Used OpenCV on the Jetson Nano for real-time face detection and age estimation. The Raspberry Pi camera module feeds frames to the GPU-accelerated Jetson for inference. Hardware integration involved mounting the camera on the chassis and routing power and signal connections between the movement platform and the compute module.

Inside the project

  • Real-time face detection and age estimation on the Jetson Nano GPU
  • Raspberry Pi camera module integration
  • Mobile chassis with motor control
  • Hardware-software co-design: mechanical assembly and embedded integration

Full Stack / Python · TCP/IP · Socket Programming · Multithreading · Client–Server Architecture · Unit Testing

Co-developed a TCP client–server application with Nicholas Sobolev for CP372, supporting currency, temperature, length, and weight conversions. Implemented a threaded server for concurrent clients and an interactive client supporting multiple requests per connection. Used a custom text protocol with request validation, formatted responses, and error handling. Currency conversions use fixed exchange rates.

The problem

Required a practical implementation of client–server networking concepts including socket programming, threading, custom protocols, and concurrent client handling.

The approach

Built a multithreaded TCP server in Python using the socket and threading modules. Each client connection is handled on a separate thread. A custom text protocol defines request formatting and response structure, with validation and error handling at both ends.

Inside the project

  • Multithreaded TCP server handling concurrent client connections
  • Currency, temperature, length, and weight conversion services
  • Custom text protocol with request validation and error handling
  • Interactive client with support for multiple requests per session
  • Unit testing for conversion logic

Robotics / Embedded Systems / HTML · JavaScript · Chart.js · ARM Assembly Concepts · Embedded Systems Simulation

Co-developed an interactive browser simulator with Samuel Okegbile to demonstrate sensor acquisition and threshold alerts using an ARM Thumb polling loop. Visualized simulated ADC readings, instruction execution, and GPIO alerts, with interactive graphs comparing Cortex-M0, M0+, M3, and M4 configurations.

The problem

ARM Cortex-M architecture concepts—polling loops, ADC acquisition, GPIO alerts—are difficult to visualize without physical hardware. Needed an accessible, browser-based tool for learning and demonstration.

The approach

Built entirely in HTML and JavaScript with Chart.js for visualization. The simulator models the Cortex-M polling loop cycle by cycle, displaying simulated ADC readings against configurable thresholds and visualizing GPIO state transitions. Comparison graphs cover four Cortex-M variants.

Inside the project

  • Interactive simulation of ARM Thumb polling loops
  • Simulated ADC readings and GPIO threshold alerts
  • Chart.js visualizations comparing Cortex-M0, M0+, M3, M4
  • Entirely browser-based, no server required

portfolioProjects.title: ASL Hand-Sign Recognition
portfolioProjects.shortDescription: Browser-based prototype recognizing static ASL hand shapes via MediaPipe and a geometric classifier.
portfolioProjects.description: Built a browser-based prototype that recognizes selected static ASL hand shapes through a webcam using MediaPipe hand tracking and a custom geometric classifier. Implemented temporal smoothing, editable subtitles, and text-to-speech. Camera frames are processed locally in the browser—no data is sent to a server.
portfolioProjects.problem: Accessibility tools for ASL recognition are often server-dependent and require significant latency. The goal was a fully client-side implementation that runs in the browser with no backend required.
portfolioProjects.approach: MediaPipe Hands provides real-time hand landmark detection in the browser. A custom geometric classifier analyzes landmark positions and angles to identify specific static hand shapes. Temporal smoothing reduces jitter. The Web Speech API drives text-to-speech output.
keyFeatures: Real-time hand landmark detection via MediaPipe in the browser

Temporal smoothing to reduce recognition jitter
Editable subtitles and Web Speech API text-to-speech

Hardware configuration and circuit rewiring for signal integrity
Iterative debugging to improve latency and responsiveness

portfolioProjects.title: Mood Project Picker
portfolioProjects.shortDescription: Self-reported preferences become a project brief through weighted matching.
portfolioProjects.description: A Flask and React project recommendation app using preference questions, difficulty selection and weighted vector similarity. It does not scientifically measure mood.
portfolioProjects.problem: Choosing a project can be harder than starting one.
portfolioProjects.approach: Match self-reported energy, creativity and challenge preferences against a project catalogue, with private browser-session history.
keyFeatures: Preference quiz and difficulty selection
Project brief and private history
Markdown export and deletion controls

portfolioProjects.title: REMNANT
portfolioProjects.shortDescription: An offline knowledge library and prerequisite-aware community skill planner.
portfolioProjects.description: A standalone Python command-line knowledge library and community skill planner with local SQLite storage. Its small example seed is a demonstration dataset.
portfolioProjects.problem: Offline information and learning dependencies need a clear, portable structure.
portfolioProjects.approach: Use local search, prerequisite graphs and validated backup/merge workflows. Core commands use the Python standard library.
keyFeatures: Offline library search
Prerequisite-aware skill planning
SQLite backups and additive snapshot merging

arm-cortex-simulator.title: Play Signal Bench
arm-cortex-simulator.note: The actual browser teaching simulator. Sensor data and timing are modeled; no physical MCU is connected.

tcp-converter.title: Try conversion logic
tcp-converter.note: A functional browser adaptation of the Python formulas and constants. The TCP server and concurrent clients are not running in this preview.

campaign-os.title: Watch actual app walkthrough
campaign-os.note: Recording from the source repository. Live generation requires a configured server, user account and provider API credentials.

arns-travel-system.title: Watch actual desktop walkthrough
arns-travel-system.note: Actual Java Swing application using example traveller data. This planner does not contact suppliers or make bookings.

remnant.title: Watch actual CLI walkthrough
remnant.note: Actual terminal commands against a temporary example database. The full project runs locally in Python.

studymind.title: Live app needs deployment
studymind.note: The API and database need hosting, account/session configuration and a server-side Claude API credential before visitors can generate material.

smart-write.title: Inference demo needs a running model API
smart-write.note: The drawing frontend needs the saved PyTorch model and a running inference service. No predictions are invented in this portfolio preview.

asl-recognition.title: Camera demo needs an HTTPS deployment
asl-recognition.note: Palm needs its Node API and same-origin MediaPipe model/WASM assets. Camera permission must be requested only after a visitor chooses to start it.

fitforge.title: Try the FitForge browser companion
fitforge.note: A functional browser companion with the native exercise catalog: build a routine, log actual sets and save local history. It is separate from the SwiftUI app and does not include Apple Health or nutrition.

hubspot-integration.title: CRM demo needs a test account
hubspot-integration.note: A public demo needs isolated sample records, a HubSpot test account, custom-object configuration and a server-side private-app token.

mood-picker.title: Live deployment needs restoring
mood-picker.note: The published Vercel URL returned DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND during this review. The Flask/React source can run locally; it needs a configured host before a live button can be enabled.

jetson-nano-robot.title: Hardware walkthrough needed
jetson-nano-robot.note: This project needs the actual robot and camera. A recording of the device working is needed for a faithful portfolio demonstration.

vex-robotics.title: Competition footage needed
vex-robotics.note: Add an actual robot or match recording to demonstrate drivetrain and control behavior. No competition footage was supplied in the current project sources.

fpv-racing-sim.title: FPV recording needed
fpv-racing-sim.note: The physical camera and viewing setup need an actual recording. No live camera feed or fabricated hardware result is shown here.
